values.value: Airport Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) and Integrated Facilities (base building 'IBF'/'IFB') with pre- and post-security T1-T2 connectors
250 Upper Domestic Loop, San Francisco, CA 94128 (Courtyard 2, between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2)

Owner/lead: SFO (City and County of SF), FAA; master/design architect HNTB (to 45 % design); architect of record Fentress Architects; design-builder Hensel Phelps; structural Walter P Moore (+ Rutherford + Chekene, Maffei Structural Engineering); MEP URS/AECOM; metal panels Keith Panel Systems (fabricator) + Pacific Erectors; glazing AGA / Wausau / Guardian / Garibaldi
siting study / FAA airspace case 2008 (site 13); construction start June 2012; structure complete Aug 2015 (WPM) / Jan 2016 (Hensel Phelps); dedication 11 Oct 2016; FAA operations from 15 Oct 2016

verification.evidence: OE/AAA case created 2008-05-06, determined 2008-08-20; 'Construction on the new tower began in June 2012' (FAA PR, AIC); 'completed in August 2015' (WPM award); Hensel Phelps completion January 2016 (43 months); dedication Tuesday 11 Oct 2016 (FAA PR dated Oct. 11, 2016; Patch 'Tuesday'); FAA use from 15 Oct 2016 (FAA PR, future tense; SFO Museum inception 2016-10-15). CTBUH: completion 2015, 12 floors (Hensel Phelps: '13-story').

values.note: 'the new tower is 221 feet tall'. Reference points NOT stated: assumed top of cab roof above local grade, excluding antennas (consistent with the photo stations below). Alternatives: 220 ft (Fentress, STRUCTURE 2017), 228 ft (early design, Archinect), 231 ft (AviationPros Dec 2015 lead; the same article's body says '221-foot', so 231 is probably a typo, not an antenna-tip height [corrected by verification]). OSM uses 67.36 m (=221 ft).

verification.evidence: 221 ft re-read in the FAA release (AviationPros copy, 11 Oct 2016), KQED, HNTB, ENR (27 Sep 2016), MCN, AIC, Patch, plus Front and CoreBrace; 220 ft in STRUCTURE and Fentress; 228 ft in Archinect. CTBUH/CVU lists 67.4 m / 221 ft as 'architectural height ... not including antennae' - a database classification of the same published number, not a survey. An independent photogrammetric test (s.12.3) puts the cab-roof rim at 63-67 m, so 'grade to roof rim' and 'grade to mast tips (rim + ~3.2 m)' both remain possible.

values.confidence: high (as an envelope) / NOT an as-built height
values.note: DOF 06-323169 (verified 'O', accuracy 4D = +-250 ft horizontal, +-50 ft vertical, lighting R, marking N, study 2008AWP00286NR, ACTION A = added, dated 2025-084 (DOF README: Action A/C = Add/Change, Julian Date = Date of Action) [corrected by verification: not an update]) carries the 2008 NRA airspace-study values: 'proposed ATCT location ... site 13 ... We will not build above 245' AMSL' (sic; the case itself is 245 AGL / 258 AMSL, site elevation 13 ft). It is the approved maximum, filed 4 years before design; use it as an upper bound only.

verification.evidence: Live OE/AAA API re-fetch of 2008-AWP-286-NRA returns the identical case (245 AGL, 13 ft site, 258 AMSL, 37.61578056 -122.38382778, created 2008-05-06, determined 2008-08-20); letter text re-read; DOF.CSV row 06-323169 identical incl. accuracy 4D (+-250 ft H, +-50 ft V per DOF_README). The description's "245' AMSL" is a template slip: sibling cases 285 (241 AGL/254 AMSL, "241' AMSL") and 287 (290 AGL/306 AMSL, "290' AMSL") repeat the AGL figure with 'AMSL', so 245 ft AGL stands.

verification.evidence: NAIP ratio re-derived from the SE-edge offsets quoted in s.4.2: 0.175-0.226 (mean 0.20), agreeing with the NCC patch ratio 0.201-0.213 -> 13.5-14.2 m at H 67.36. But the photo span puts the airside parapet at 17.5 m for {H 67.36, D 14.3} (16.3 m for D 14.75). The spec's own trio {h_roof_top 67.36, d_cab_roof 14.3, h_ibf_roof 14.2} fails this check by ~3 m; the 147-ft ribbon 'ends at the flare' argument does not discriminate (it fits several combinations).

Outer edge of the cab-roof cap (widest, at the top). (a) Famartin 11:57 photo: 480 px at 0.0299 m/px, the scale coming from the published 11-ft cab glass panel seen at its measured 20 deg outward slope (105 px = 3.14 m) -> 14.35 m; (b) Google 03dcd4ae top view circle fit r 7.1-7.7 m (reference only); (c) NAIP circle fits r 6.0-7.6 m (0.6 m GSD, low contrast); (d) OSM cab polygon r 7.7-8.1 m.

verification.evidence: (a) The 11-ft-panel scale projects the near-side glass as 11 ft x cos(20.4 deg); seen from 13 deg below, the near-side projection is 11 ft x cos(20.4 - 13.1 deg) = 0.99 x 11 ft, and the limb widths are ~2.5 % farther than the near-side glass -> the same pixels give ~15.5 m if the whole 11-ft panel is visible (less if the frame hides part of it). (b) Google is reference-only; (c) OSM is traced from lean-affected imagery. Independent: EXIF focal length + GPS on two Famartin iPhone photos from opposite sides: 14.27 (11:57) and 15.21 m (09:12:13) at x -739, mean 14.74-14.76 m for any cab x in -744..-734 -> 14.75 +- 0.5 m. NAIP bright-disc edge is ambiguous (50 % crossings r 6.0-7.75; a faint ring at r 6.5-7.0).

values.value: round airside body (flared hyperboloid-like 'torch'), opened on the landside/west face into a recessed glass ribbon flanked by two curved blades (fins); one blade ends at the top in a sharp prow projecting beyond the round flare; the ribbon faces the upper-level roadway / AirTrain (towards ~WNW-NW, approx. bearing 300-320 deg).
values.note: 'opening of the tower shell to expose the core with a backlit glass facade, which greets passengers arriving along the upper-level roadway and SFO's AirTrain' (HNTB, MCN 2017). Exact fin plan geometry: open question.
'147 foot-tall ribbon of glass'; AIC: 'nearly 150 vertical feet of glass'. With IBF roof 14.2 m it ends at ~59 m, i.e. at the flare top (consistent).

verification.evidence: 147 ft re-read in the FAA release, KQED, MCN ('west facade') and AviationPros 2015; AIC 'nearly 150 feet'. Its start and end levels are not published; with D = 14.75 m the photo span parapet -> flare top is 3.01 D = 44.4 m = 146 ft.

values.note: T2 AirTrain 2018 photo (near-frontal): 28 px -> 60 px vs cab roof 125 px; trapezoid widening upwards. Mullion grid ~2 columns (bottom) to ~3 (top), row pitch ~1.8 m (count ~25 rows) - approximate.

values.value: west facade ('landside'); LED backlit, programmable colour-changing ('waterfall'); Wausau four-sided silicone-glazed curtainwall (SuperWall 8250, INvision 7250-UW unitized, 7250 BHM), Guardian SunGuard SNX 62/27 IGUs by Garibaldi Glass; > 4,000 sq ft curtainwall (tower)

about 1,500 curved, trapezoidal metal wall panels with spiralling (rotated) joints; 10,000 sq ft of formable 4-mm Alucobond Plus ACM in custom 'SFO Silver' on the KPS System A pressure-equalized rainscreen; lightning-discharge system woven into the panel seams
values.note: STRUCTURE 2017 calls it 'brushed aluminum cladding'. Our photo-derived envelope (IBF roof to flare top) is ~1,900 m2 = ~20,000 sq ft, twice the published ACM area -> open question (partial figure, or smaller tower).

verification.evidence: MCN: ~1,500 panels (Keith Panel Systems), 10,000 sq ft of Alucobond (Pacific Erectors). Front Inc.: flat panels cold-curved in one direction, faceting in the other.

values.note: FAA: '650 square-foot controller work area'. Our glass-bottom diameter 10.0 m gives ~79 m2 (850 sq ft) gross inside the glass line: plausible net of the core/stair penetrations.
Different quantities are probably being described (glazed arc vs mullion-free arc vs usable view). Needs a plan drawing.

roof cantilevered from a 2'-2" x 3'-4" center column of 1 1/2" steel plate (14 tons); three 2'-0" x 1'-4" landside columns hold the cantilevered roof in tension

values.value: slip-formed cast-in-place reinforced-concrete cylinder, unbonded vertical post-tensioning (26 tendon bundles) for self-centring; >1,100 cu yd concrete; steel-framed flare and cab cantilever from the core; 2 tuned mass dampers near the cab; performance-based seismic design (operational at DE, M 7.5-8)
values.note: Snippet-only extras (archmag_snippet, low): core 30 in thick at base, 18 in at top; 19 cables x 7 strands per bundle; '200-foot high concrete core'. TMD mass: 2 x ~37,000 lb (AviationPros) vs '35,000-pound weights on all four sides' (AIC) vs 75,000 lb total (SF Chronicle via STRUCTURE).

verification.evidence: STRUCTURE: vertically post-tensioned, slip-formed core; flare and cab steel; four horizontal buckling-restrained braces as a backstay (CoreBrace: 4 welded BRBs); TMDs near the cab. ENR: 26 vertical PT cables, >1,100 cu yd. Architect Magazine still HTTP 403 (and Wayback 429) - snippet items remain unverified.
